blocks.text: मृदुमध्याधिमात्रत्वात्ततोऽपि विशेषः । २२ । Mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāttato'pi viśeṣaḥ /I.22/ Mṛdu-madhya-adhimātratvāt tato'pi viśeṣaḥ/I.22/
“And it is even closer according as the intensity [of the drive] is mild, moderate, or extreme.”

Mṛdu-tīvro madhya-tīvro'dhimātra-tīvra iti, tato'pi viśeṣaḥ / Tad-viśeṣān 629 mṛdu- tīvrasaṃvegasya_āsannas tato madhya-tīvra-saṃvegasya_āsannataras tasmād adhimātra-tīvrasaṃvegasya_adhimātra-upāyasya_āsannatamaḥ samādhi-lābhaḥ 630 samādhi-phalaṃ ca_iti /22/

[Gloss] The compound Mṛdumadhyādhimātra is a dvandva of which each term qualifies tīvra ‘intensity’ [of the drive], so that the meaning is: according as the intensity [of the drive] is mild, moderate, or extreme, [the closeness of samādhi] is even greater.

Depending on this degree [of intensity], the attainment of mental enstasis as well as its fruit is close for one whose drive is mildly intense, closer for one whose drive is moderately intense, and closest for one who employs extreme means with a drive of extreme intensity 631. /22/
629 D and Maas 2006a: 33: viśeṣād api mṛdu°.
630 MAAS 2006a: 33: tadviśeṣād apy āsannataras tīvrādhimātrasya samādhilābhaḥ.

631 By combining the two sūtra, Vijñāna Bhikṣu arrives at eighty-one varieties of drive. This kind of calculation is highly appreciated in the Brahmanical tradition. Among other examples, Abhinavagupta (Tantrāloka, chap. XIII) presents a table of the intensity of divine grace (anugraha, śaktipāta) using almost the same vocabulary as the bhāṣyakāra (tīvra ‘intense’, madhya ‘medium’, and manda ‘weak’). He distinguishes nine of them, from tīvratīvra ‘very intense’ (literally ‘intensely intense’) to mandamanda ‘very weak’.
